title: Agent Reinforcement Fine Tuning – Will Hang & Cathy Zhou, OpenAI
talk_summary: OpenAI's fine-tuning team explains agent reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT), where a model explores tool-calling trajectories against a custom reward endpoint to learn domain-specific tool use. Customer case studies (Cognition, Codium, Cosine, Macco) show gains in tool-call efficiency, latency stability, and reward-hacking defenses.

takeaways.what_they_do: Cosine gave reward only when final code passes tests, not partial credit for style/tone, because partial credit made the model optimize cosmetics; Macco built a judge to catch 7 observed reward-hacking patterns and an AST check that kernels actually exist and launch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they give the model the reward only when the final code passes the test

takeaways.what_they_do: Cosine's grader rewarded agents that validate their own work — running tests, inspecting terminal output, checking lint — before declaring success.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the grader will reward the agents that validate their own work

takeaways.what_they_do: Macco ran three samples and took the best, beating state-of-the-art by 72%.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They ran three different samples and they took the best one out of the three

takeaways.what_they_do: They penalize the model for exceeding a tool-call budget, and it learns to stay within budget while preserving accuracy; long-tail runs (>15 tool calls, >100 messages) collapsed to 2-4.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can actually impose this penalty that you know penalizes the model for going over that budget
takeaways.numbers: long-tail >15 tool calls eliminated; converged to 2-4

takeaways.what_they_do: They insist eval and training sets match production traffic with no drift, and establish a base-model baseline before optimizing.
RFT taught the agent to launch many tool calls in parallel at step one, cutting 8-10 sequential steps to 4.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent launches many tool calls in parallel at the very first step
